WinPopup P2P native dependencies
================================

Built for Windows x64 using MSVC 19.44 and the static release C runtime (/MT).
No audio/video codecs are compiled into Tox. The installed static libraries
produce an executable requiring Windows system DLLs only.

Versions and origins
-------------------
c-toxcore 0.2.23 (GPL-3.0-or-later)
https://github.com/TokTok/c-toxcore/releases/tag/v0.2.23
Archive: c-toxcore-v0.2.23.tar.gz
SHA256: 15cdd006ed7793dfc657e340ef9f218f6637d2fe5b130704d39b961389bb6cd6
This official release archive contains the corresponding source, including CMP.
Its hash matches GitHub's release asset digest. No Tox source was modified.

CMP (MIT)
The exact revision bundled by the c-toxcore 0.2.23 full source release is used.
https://github.com/TokTok/cmp

libsodium 1.0.22 (ISC)
https://download.libsodium.org/libsodium/releases/
Source archive: libsodium-1.0.22.tar.gz
SHA256: adbdd8f16149e81ac6078a03aca6fc03b592b89ef7b5ed83841c086191be3349
Official MSVC binary archive: libsodium-1.0.22-msvc.zip
SHA256: 3e03a726fac4bc09cb61d8f29d658ef7a5eca0811de59082130414f7ca2e4279
The x64/Release/v143/static library is used. The source archive contains
builds/msvc/vs2022/libsodium.sln to rebuild it with Visual Studio 2022;
select x64 / StaticRelease. Both archives were fetched using official HTTPS.

pthreads4w 3.0.0 (Apache-2.0)
https://sourceforge.net/projects/pthreads4w/
Archive: pthreads4w-code-v3.0.0.zip
SHA512: 49e541b66c26ddaf812edb07b61d0553e2a5816ab002edc53a38a897db8ada6d0a096c98a9af73a8f40c94283df53094f76b429b09ac49862465d8697ed20013
Hash independently matches Microsoft's vcpkg port. Source was built with
nmake VC-static in an MSVC x64 environment. No source modifications.

Build
-----
Install Visual Studio 2022 with Desktop development with C++ and its CMake
tools, then run in PowerShell:

    .\build-dependencies.ps1

The script imports the x64 compiler environment, verifies archives, extracts
them into this dependency directory and builds Tox + pthreads4w. It uses
the official static libsodium binary. Missing archives are downloaded.
Build output goes into build-nmake; installed headers, libraries and license
texts go into install. The script supports -VisualStudioPath for custom installs.

NMake Makefiles are used to avoid MSBuild's SDK discovery on restricted hosts.
The top-level CMakeLists.txt uses the exact production source list in the
upstream Tox CMake file and adds toxencryptsave. Source files remain unchanged.

Consumer link settings
----------------------
Include directory: install/include
Libraries: install/lib/toxcore.lib, libsodium.lib, pthreadVC3.lib
Windows libraries: ws2_32, iphlpapi, advapi32, bcrypt
Consumer C runtime: /MT
Consumer define: SODIUM_STATIC
If including pthread.h directly, also define __PTW32_STATIC_LIB.

Verification
------------
dependency-smoke.c was built and executed successfully against these libraries:
  Tox 0.2.23; libsodium 1.0.22
  toxencryptsave encrypt/decrypt round trip
  Tox creation, iteration and teardown (UDP disabled for this unit smoke test)
The application-level integration tests separately verify peer messaging.

Suggested source distribution contents
--------------------------------------
Include CMakeLists.txt, build-dependencies.ps1, DEPENDENCIES.txt,
dependency-smoke.c, install/, and these complete source archives:
  c-toxcore-v0.2.23.tar.gz
  libsodium-1.0.22.tar.gz
  pthreads4w-code-v3.0.0.zip

The large libsodium MSVC archive may be omitted from the source package;
the dependency build script downloads and verifies it when rebuilding.
The bundled install/ static libraries let users compile the app immediately.

Bootstrap nodes
---------------
bootstrap-nodes.json is a snapshot from https://nodes.tox.chat/json fetched on
30 September 2026. The application pins selected node DHT public keys; it
does not silently fetch untrusted replacement node keys on startup.
Public bootstrap peers allow first contact with the Tox DHT. TCP relay peers
help when a direct UDP connection cannot be established. Neither component
provides offline message storage. Endpoints still need to be online together.

No infrastructure to operate is possible for users of the public Tox network.
Zero infrastructure dependency across arbitrary NATs is not a truthful claim:
discovery needs reachable peers and some network combinations require relays.
The app can support direct connections where the network permits them.
